newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia considers 16 as homosexual age of consent.
newsitem.headline: Australia considers 16 as homosexual age of consent.

text.p: Australia will consider new laws making 16 the national age of consent for homosexuals and jailing paedophiles for up to 25 years.
A discussion paper presented to the government on Friday aimed to standardise sex laws across Australia, local media said on Saturday.

The paper suggested setting an age of consent for females and males at 16, regardless of whether the act was heterosexual or homosexual, because the ages ranged from 16 to 18 in Australia's six states and two territories.
"The age of consent should be the same whether the activity is heterosexual or homosexual," The Australian newspaper quoted the discussion paper as saying.

"The inference that might be drawn from an older age of consent for homosexual conduct is that homosexual activity is an undesirable activity from which males should be both protected and deterred until adulthood," says the paper by lawmakers.
The state of Tasmania is the only state with anti-homosexual laws. The Tasmanian law carries a maximum term of 25 years in jail.
The discussion paper also recommends that a 25-year jail term be imposed on paedophiles, three years for stalkers and 15 years for female genital mutilation, The Australian said.

The discussion paper also said the law should allow for a defence of having a reasonable belief that the child was over the age of consent, a victim's sexual history should not be used as evidence and that judges should not be able to warn or suggest children in sexual cases were unreliable witnesses.
The paper was prepared by a committee of national, state and territory attorneys-general.
